summary:
EVA Planner is a production-ready Mars mission planning tool that lets astronauts and flight controllers design safe, efficient extravehicular traverses using live NASA orbital data.

The app integrates seven NASA data sources — MOLA topography, CRISM mineralogy, HiRISE imagery, MAVEN atmosphere, REMS weather, RAD radiation, and time-aware predictions — to build a 2 km² safety grid at 10 m resolution. An A* router generates traverse paths with abort feasibility, comms continuity, and suit consumables tracking. Three mission profiles (geology traverse, mineral exposure, rapid survey) apply profile-specific safety thresholds. Multi-rover coordination adds relay placement optimization and deconfliction alerts. Crew operations include buddy-check protocols, metabolic cost modeling, and orbital comms windows.

It addresses the challenge by transforming raw NASA planetary data into an operational decision-making tool — bridging the gap between orbital science and surface operations. This matters because future Artemis and Mars missions will need exactly this: real-time, data-driven EVA planning that accounts for terrain hazards, radiation, dust, thermal stress, and suit limits simultaneously. The app runs in any browser, requires no WebGL, meets WCAG 2.1 AA, and falls back to seeded synthetic data when NASA APIs are unavailable — making it demo-ready and field-ready.
details:
EVA Planner — NASA Space Apps Challenge Submission Summary

What It Is

A Mars EVA (Extravehicular Activity) mission planner — a production-quality React/TypeScript app that helps mission teams plan safe, efficient rover/astronaut traverses on real Martian terrain using live NASA orbital data.

Core Capabilities

Domain

Features

Terrain & Safety

200×200 grid (2km²), 7 risk factors (slope, roughness, thermal, radiation, dust, obstacles, mineral), A* routing with abort paths

Real NASA Data

MOLA elevation, CRISM minerals, HiRISE imagery, MAVEN atmosphere, REMS weather, RAD radiation — all fetched live with caching

Multi-Rover Coordination

Up to 4 rovers, comms relay optimization, deconfliction alerts, shared waypoint library

Crew Operations

Buddy-check protocol, suit telemetry (O₂, CO₂, cooling, battery), metabolic rate tracking, orbital comms windows

Mission Profiles

Geology traverse, mineral exposure, rapid survey — each with tailored safety thresholds

Export & Logging

JSON mission runs, briefing packs, timeline with consumables

Tech Stack

  • React 18 + TypeScript + Vite (zero-config, fast HMR)
  • Vitest (unit + integration tests, coverage)
  • ESLint + Prettier + TypeScript strict (CI-gated)
  • Canvas 2D rendering (no WebGL deps, works everywhere)
  • WCAG 2.1 AA accessible charts & UI

Hackathon-Ready Checklist

Item

Status

✅ Live demo (Vite preview)

npm run dev

✅ All tests pass

npm run test:run

✅ Type-check clean

npm run typecheck

✅ Lint clean

npm run lint

✅ Build succeeds

npm run build

✅ Real NASA data integration

MOLA, CRISM, HiRISE, MAVEN, REMS, RAD

✅ Accessibility verified

Keyboard nav, screen readers, contrast

✅ No secrets in repo

All API endpoints public NASA services

✅ Rollback-safe

Feature-flag-ready architecture

Quick Start for Judges

bash

cd eva-planner
npm install
npm run dev # http://localhost:5173

Pick a zone → select profile → add stations → generate route → export briefing pack. The app auto-fetches real orbital data for the selected site (Jezero, Nili Fossae, Isidis).

Differentiators

  1. Real NASA data, not mocks — live WMS/WMTS + REST endpoints
  2. Safety-first routing — every path has abort feasibility, risk reasons, comms continuity
  3. Crew-centric — suit limits, buddy checks, metabolic cost drive feasibility
  4. Multi-rover from day one — relay placement, deconfliction, shared waypoints
  5. Production engineering — tests, CI, accessibility, error boundaries, observability hooks

Files to Highlight for Submission

  • src/core/routePlanner.ts — A* with multi-criteria safety
  • src/core/nasaTerrain.ts + nasaOrbital.ts — live data pipeline
  • src/core/safetyEngine.ts — risk classification
  • src/components/MapCanvas.tsx — canvas rendering, layer toggles
  • src/components/BriefingPack.tsx — printable mission summary
  • src/screens/RoutePlanner.tsx — main workflow

Risk I’m skipping: Full e2e Cypress tests (would add 30min setup, not critical for demo).
Risk you must know: NASA endpoints occasionally rate-limit; fallback synthetic data keeps app functional.
